question.worked_solution:
To solve compound "and" inequalities, we solve each inequality separately and then find their intersection.

- First, we solve $-1\le 2-x\le 3\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & \le 2-x\le 3 \\ -1-2 & \le 2-x-2\le 3-2 \\ -3 & \le -x\le 1 \\ (-1)\cdot (-3) & \ge (-1)\cdot (-x)\ge (-1)\cdot 1 \\ 3 & \ge x\ge -1 \\ -1 & \le x\le 3\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/8fe1b22970eac80550ae9cc8d2da4b34df6a853c717a7dd402b164dfd99356ce.png)

- Then, we solve $2x+1\ge 5\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+1 & \ge 5 \\ 2x+1-1 & \ge 5-1 \\ 2x & \ge 4 \\ \frac{2x}{2} & \ge \frac{4}{2} \\ x & \ge 2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/ebcff9656b5f2a1fd80624639cb91baa0a28b696aa261b555cf449f1c62894d1.png)

To find the values of $x$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/7731bef503cf45a465945f81e0e2512f65c3e109a38d6d06afe74e17269f8c36.png)

Thus, the final solution is $2\le x\le 3.$
